_comment: #508. Italian flats: Mediterranean rather than Victorian, so the Base field is plaster - ochre,
wheat, a warm terracotta-tinted cream, one cool grey-green for relief, and an ivory. Warmer than
Noe Valley across the board and noticeably less grey than the belt.
The identifying move is Accent1: cream, and a bottle green for the shutters and door leaves. It
is the only palette in the library with a saturated green in Accent1 and it is what makes a
North Beach block read as North Beach. Accent2 ramps a plaster tan into a deeper ochre for
sills, hoods and the cornice band.
Sign is authored (an Italian-red awning/board note) - north_beach_flats is residential, but the
ground floor of that stock is shopfronts more often than not.
Authored, not verified in an Editor.
